subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Dramatic Impact Movement And Entertainment
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The concerto grosso typically contrasts which two performing groups?
questions.explain: The Baroque concerto grosso opposes a small group of soloists (concertino) against the full ensemble (ripieno or tutti).

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A major seventh chord on the tonic
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: A plagal cadence consists of which progression?
questions.explain: The plagal ('Amen') cadence moves from the subdominant (IV) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: The music has no fixed pulse
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
The lyrics printed beneath a song
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
Recording the score before filming begins
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: In ensemble performance, good 'ensemble skills' include all of the following EXCEPT...?
options: Maintaining a shared sense of pulse
Listening and balancing dynamics with other players
Watching for cues and breathing together
Deliberately ignoring the other performers' tempo
questions.explain: Strong ensemble playing depends on listening, balancing and keeping together, not ignoring fellow performers.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: The compositional device of 'augmentation' refers to...?
options: Lengthening the note values of a theme, usually doubling them
Raising the pitch of a theme
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens a theme's note values, typically doubling each duration.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: Mozart's 'The Marriage of Figaro' is an example of which operatic genre?
questions.explain: 'Le nozze di Figaro' is a comic opera (opera buffa) by Mozart.

questions.q: 'Sequencing' in music production primarily involves...?
options: Adding distortion to a guitar amplifier
Arranging musical events (often MIDI) in time on a DAW timeline for playback or editing
Mastering a finished album for vinyl
questions.explain: Sequencing arranges and edits musical events, frequently MIDI data, along a timeline for playback.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: A 'riff' in rock and pop music is best defined as...?
options: A short, repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern, often instrumental
questions.explain: A riff is a short, catchy pattern repeated throughout a song, frequently as an instrumental hook.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
A swung shuffle feel in the bass
Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: A 'drone' as a textural device (e.g. in Indian or Celtic music) is...?
options: A sustained note or notes held continuously beneath the melody
questions.explain: A drone is a continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) underpinning the melody.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: A slow, free and unmetred mood
A return to the opening alap
A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
Silence with only the drone sounding
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: In a 'verse-chorus' pop structure, a 'pre-chorus' serves to...?
options: Build anticipation and lead smoothly from the verse into the chorus
questions.explain: The pre-chorus builds momentum and links the verse to the chorus.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.
